- Wait for scientific consensus

One reason for this position is that conducting welfare assessments prematurely can lead to misattributions and misinterpretations of AI behavior, which can have significant ethical and practical implications. Without a solid scientific consensus, these assessments may be unreliable and could result in unnecessary ethical dilemmas and resource misallocations.

- Wait for scientific consensus

One reason for this position is that conducting welfare assessments prematurely can lead to misattributions and misinterpretations of AI behavior, which could result in unrealistic expectations and ethical dilemmas. Until there is a scientific consensus on what constitutes welfare-relevant states in AI, assessments may be unreliable and could cause more harm than good.

- Start assessing now

One reason for this position is that starting assessments now allows developers to begin gathering data and developing methodologies, which can contribute to the eventual scientific consensus. Early engagement can help identify potential issues and inform the scientific community, accelerating the development of reliable and valid assessment tools.
